title: Staged diagnostic retry policy and quarantine collector
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds staged retry/backoff policy for diagnostic probes, quarantined collector for failing artifacts, and CLI controls; opt-in by default for controlled rollout.
commits: staged-retry: implement backoff state machine and basic policy (Maya)
quarantine: local quarantine store and TTL eviction (Maya)
cli: diagctl commands to inspect and release quarantined payloads (Maya)
tests: unit and integration harness for retry/backoff and file-based quarantine (Tests team)
docs: usage notes and rollout plan (Maya)
fix: idempotency token handling and metrics labels (Priya)
ci: stabilize flaky test by adding deterministic clock mock (Lars)
description: Context: Production diagnostic probes (oncall responders and automated runbook samplers) occasionally produce backpressure on telemetry pipelines when a cluster-wide issue causes repeated failures. This leads to bursts of retry traffic that amplify the underlying problem and generates noise for oncall. Motivation: introduce a safe, observable mechanism to stage retries and quarantine failing diagnostic payloads so we can preserve signal while preventing retry storms. Design summary: implemented a two-stage retry policy (fast path exponential backoff for transient errors, then staged retries with an increasing hold time) plus a local quarantine collector that snapshots failed payloads to an append-only store with TTL and controlled re-ingest. The quarantine store is filesystem-backed by default and supports optional S3 backend via configuration. Key invariants: idempotency tokens are required for replays, quarantined items have metadata (first_failure_ts, attempts, last_error) and are observable via metrics and CLI. Opt-in rollout: default behavior is controlled by the new config flag diag.staged_retry.enabled=false; we're enabling for internal CI-only initially and plan gradual ramp to 10% production traffic as a Linear task. Checklist: - [x] Add retry state machine and unit tests - [x] Add quarantine store with TTL and eviction tests - [x] Add diagctl commands: list, inspect, release, delete - [x] Emit metrics: diag.quarantine.size, diag.retry.attempts, diag.retry.latency_hist - [x] Add config and helm values, default to off - [x] Add docs and rollout plan - [x] Pass CI and e2e harness Notes on changes and files: retry_policy.py contains the BackoffStateMachine with deterministic mocks for tests; collector.py wires staged retry into the sampling loop and defers to quarantine_store on persistent failures; quarantine_store.py implements append-only segments with compact TTL sweeps and an index for quick lookups; diagctl exposes inspection and safe-release operations which require a confirmation token to prevent accidental mass replays. Tests: added both unit tests and a small integration harness (scripts/perf/run_diag_harness.sh) that simulates transient and persistent failure modes. I reproduced the flaky behavior from the incident report in ENG-5823 locally and validated the quarantine prevents retry amplification without losing payloads. Review conversation (condensed into single narrative): Priya requested clearer semantics around idempotency tokens and safe-release; I updated the API and added stronger validation and a CLI confirmation token. Lars flagged a flaky test in the e2e harness (timing-dependent); I introduced a deterministic clock mock and the CI run passed. Zoe asked for more granular metrics labels to separate probe-type and tenant; added diag.probe_type label and a migration note in the docs. CI history: initial run showed one flaky test failure in test_quarantine_store related to sleep timing; after introducing clock mock and re-running, all checks passed (unit, lint, mypy, integration harness). Performance: microbenchmarks show median latency impact on the probe path <2ms when staged retry is disabled; when enabled in staging with small queue sizes, end-to-end throughput for probes decreased by ~1.6% under heavy failure load but overall error amplification reduced by ~72%. Safety and operational considerations: quarantine store has an admin-only retention policy and an automated TTL sweep; admins can delete or replay individual items via diagctl; replay requires confirmation token and respects original idempotency token so duplicate replays are safe. Migration and rollout: 1) Merge to main (this PR) 2) Enable diag.staged_retry.enabled=true in internal staging and monitor diag.quarantine.size, diag.retry.attempts, diag.retry.failures 3) Gradual 10/30/60/100% rollout across regions with on-call watch window and automatic rollback flag. Rollback plan: flip diag.staged_retry.enabled=false and optionally purge quarantined items older than retention window if necessary. Merge details: squash-merged into main by Lars Holm on 2025-11-02 after approvals from Priya and Zoe. Follow-ups: ENG-6041 to add S3-backed quarantines with encryption-at-rest and KMS integration, and ENG-6110 to add a retention UI in Redwood Console.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps staged retry off by default; config and helm values included for controlled rollout. No breaking changes to public SDK surface. CLI has an extra confirmation knob to prevent accidental replay.
examples: To inspect quarantine: diagctl quarantine list --limit 50
To release an item: diagctl quarantine release --id a1b2c3 --confirm-token <token>
